Last week, I again voted against a partisan recissions package that embodies Washington, D.C.’s misplaced priorities.

This legislation failed to offer a real, long-term strategy to root out waste, fraud, and abuse in federal programs or to cut red tape so civil servants can do their jobs more effectively.

This lack of lasting action comes at a time when the Appropriations Committee advanced a bill I voted against that will defund our federal auditing watchdog by 50%.

I would have preferred a strategic rebalancing of the clipboards to work boots ratio in our federal spending, with appropriately tailored savings on nonessential programs, instead of cuts that will negatively affect our community.

This legislation guts lifesaving emergency alert systems rural communities rely on, impacts public programs for kids that can be a better alternative to AI slop online, and leaves Ukrainians out to dry in their fight against despotism – at the cost of our own national security.

Despite the bipartisan support for releasing the Epstein files, this package fails to require the Administration to do just that and finally give the American people the transparency they’re demanding.

It’s disrespectful to folks in my community who want to know that the rich and powerful are held to the same standards that they are.

This package is an attempt to draw attention away from the budget reconciliation law I voted against that will explode our national debt by $4 trillion.

And it’s only lip service to the urgent need to have a federal government that stewards our hard-earned tax dollars and delivers for SW Washington in a cost-effective way.

Many Americans believe Jesus calls us to bear one another’s burdens — Chaplains like Mark take that real seriously. They volunteer their time to make sure our neighbors are spared from facing some of the worst news of their lives alone.

When I learned that it’s easier to fund a chatbot for mental health support than reimburse volunteer chaplains for their gas money I wanted to change that. And we did. 

Thank you to Mark and his brothers and sisters in service. It was a real privilege to have you join me at the State of the Union.

It's shocking, but Senator Braun voted against HB 2225, a bill that puts common-sense restrictions on technology companies from sending sexually explicit material to children through AI companion chatbots. And now he's lying about it. It's clear who Braun works for and it's not us.
was one of just a few people in the state Legislature to vote against a bill that would have prohibited technology companies from providing sexually explicit material for children in an AI bill.

Repeatedly, John Braun denied voting against House Bill 2225 — the law that stops AI chatbots from engaging in sexually explicit conversations with kids. At our last debate, he went further. He claimed the bill didn’t exist and his vote “never happened." Pressed by the Seattle Times, he now admits that he DID vote no on protecting Washington’s children from predatory AI. Thankfully, the bill passed anyway, Braun didn’t just cast a bad vote. He lied about it, repeatedly. If he’ll rewrite his record on something this clear, what else is he hiding?

During last week’s debate, I confronted my opponent, John Braun, about his despicable vote against legislation designed to protect children from sexually explicit content generated by AI chatbots. [...] These are basic protections for our children in a world where technology advances faster than parents can keep up.

Well, one of the big deals, the Big Beautiful Bill that passed at the beginning of this Congress gave millions of dollars of tax credits to data centers. That needs to be rescinded and revoked. And we need to have a federal policy that ensures that ordinary people are held harmless, that we're not impacted by the energy, water use, the noise, weird noise pollution, that communities are held harmless when data centers are developed.

And also, as a mom, real concerns. I know your question's about data centers, but it's also about AI and what its impacts are on children. As a mom, I have real concerns. My opponent voted against a bill that would have prevented AI chatbots from delivering sexually explicit material to children.
